LESSON: CURRENT ELECTRICITY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: PHYSICS FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Electricity and Magnetism
Topic 3.2: Current Electricity
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Current Electricity, part of Electricity and Magnetism in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 PHYSICS FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How is current electricity applicable in our day to day life? 2. Why are resistors used in electrical circuits?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Current Electricity together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and Problem Solving: the learner develops the evaluation and decision making skill while they

explore complex problems while deriving the mathematical relationship between emf, potential difference, electric

current, resistance and use it to solve related problems.

• Learning to learn: the learner develops the skill of carrying out research as they perform an experiment to investigate

the relationship between potential difference and current through a conductor and draw the requisite graphs.

Values

• Responsibility: as the learner takes accountability as they care for their own property and those of peers while

performing experiments with peers to investigate the factors affecting resistance of Ohmic resistors.

• Respect: the learner acquires communication etiquette by displaying humility during discussions and practical

sessions.
